question: 33-year-old man without a history of interest. These symptoms suggest a potential diagnosis of alcohol use disorder and possibly bipolar disorder due to the reported mood swings. The reasoning chain for attention deficit disorder (ADD) is weak, as the symptoms of distractibility and forgetfulness are more likely secondary to alcohol use and mood instability rather than primary ADD. Adaptive disorder is also less likely given the chronicity and complexity of the symptoms.
